problems.title: Cone volume from perpendicular generators
problems.question: Two perpendicular generators divide a cone’s base circumference in ratio 1:2. The height is 2√2. Find its volume.
problems.idea: The arc ratio fixes the central angle at 120°.
formulas: For apex-to-base generator vectors, dot product=h²+r²cos120°.
steps: Perpendicularity gives h²-r²/2=0, so r²=2h².
With h=2√2, r²=16.
The volume is π·16·2√2/3=32π√2/3.

problems.title: Differentiate a double-angle expression
problems.question: f(x)=sin2x+2cos²x. Find f′(π/12).
problems.idea: Apply the chain rule, then evaluate double angles.
steps: f′(x)=2cos2x-4sinx cosx=2cos2x-2sin2x.
At x=π/12, the doubled angle is π/6.

problems.title: Domain of a logarithmic square root
problems.question: Find the domain of y=√(-8(log₉x)²+log₁/₃x+3).
problems.idea: Use t=log₉x and require a nonnegative radicand.
formulas: A real logarithm needs x>0; a real square root needs radicand ≥0.
steps: The condition is -8t²-2t+3≥0.
Factor its negative: (4t+3)(2t-1)≤0, giving -3/4≤t≤1/2.
The increasing base 9 gives 9^(-3/4)≤x≤3.
Since 9^(-3/4)=1/(3√3), this gives the interval below.

problems.title: Cylinder height from a tilted pair of equal chords
problems.question: Parallel chords AB,CD lie in opposite bases of a cylinder of radius 3. Both chords have length 4. Their common plane makes 60° with a base. Find the cylinder volume.
problems.idea: The equal chords have equal centre distances; the nonvertical section forces their projections to lie on opposite sides of the centre.
steps: Each chord is √(9-4)=√5 from the base centre.
If their projections coincided, the section would be vertical, contradicting 60°. Thus their horizontal separation is 2√5.
The height is h=2√5tan60°=2√15.
The volume is π·9·2√15=18π√15 cm³.

problems.title: Two chain-rule and product-rule derivatives
problems.question: Differentiate (a) y=(arccos(x^(1/4)))³; (b) y=(eˣ+lnx)log₅x.
problems.idea: For (a), differentiate from the outside inward. For (b), apply the product rule.
steps: (a) The function domain is 0≤x≤1. On 0<x<1, multiply the derivatives of the cube, arccosine and fourth root.
(b) For x>0, the first factor’s derivative is eˣ+1/x, and the second factor’s derivative is 1/(xln5).
The product derivative is (eˣ+1/x)log₅x+(eˣ+lnx)/(xln5).

problems.title: Increasing and decreasing intervals with a fifth root
problems.question: Find monotonicity intervals of y=√[5]((x+3)⁴)·(x-2)⁵.
problems.idea: Keep the sign of the real fifth root when differentiating.
steps: Use the product rule: the bracket after taking common factors is (4/5)(x-2)+5(x+3)=(29x+67)/5.
Apart from x=2, the derivative sign is the sign of (29x+67)/(x+3).
For x<-3 both numerator and denominator are negative, so y increases. For -3<x<-67/29 the derivative is negative, so y decreases.
For x>-67/29 it is positive except at the isolated stationary input 2, so the function increases throughout that interval.
The derivative is undefined at -3, but the function itself is continuous there.

problems.title: Rotate an obtuse isosceles triangle about a leg
problems.question: An isosceles triangle with equal sides 4 cm and base 6 cm rotates about one equal side. Find the solid volume.
problems.idea: The perpendicular foot of the third vertex lies outside the rotation segment; use the difference of two cones.
formulas: Perpendicular distance to the rotation axis ρ=2Δ/axis length.
The difference of cone volumes is πρ² times the difference of their heights, divided by 3.
steps: The triangle’s base altitude is √(4²-3²)=√7, so Δ=3√7.
The distance from the other vertex to the axis is ρ=2Δ/4=3√7/2.
The two cones have the same base radius ρ, and their heights differ by the rotation-side length 4. Their difference is the rotated triangle’s solid.

problems.title: An axial-diagonal angle needs an orientation
problems.question: A conical frustum’s axial diagonals divide each other 2:1 and have an angle of 120° between them. Each diagonal is 3 m. Find the volume.
problems.idea: Express a diagonal using its horizontal projection R+r and vertical projection h.
steps: If the specified 120° is between the upward rays, then h²-(R+r)²=-9/2. Together with their squared sum 9, this gives h=3/2 and R+r=3√3/2.
Thus r=√3/2,R=√3, and V=21π/8 m³.
Without identifying the rays, the diagonals also have a 120° supplementary angle when the upward-ray angle is 60°. That case gives h=3√3/2, r=1/2,R=1, and V=7√3π/8 m³.
Both configurations have the stated diagonal length and a 120° angle at the intersection. A labelled angle would select one.
problems.answer: Upward-ray interpretation: 21π/8 m³. With no ray orientation specified, 7√3π/8 m³ is also possible.
problems.note: The source gives no diagram identifying which of the intersection angles is meant, so both geometric possibilities are recorded.

problems.title: A cosine-difference limit
problems.question: Find lim as x→0 of (cos3x-cosx)/x².
problems.idea: Convert the numerator into a product of sines.
formulas: lim(t→0) sint/t=1, with angles in radians.
steps: The numerator is -2sin2x sinx.
Divide as -4[sin2x/(2x)][sinx/x].
Each bracket tends to 1, so the limit is -4.

problems.title: Opposite-sign exponential-equation roots
problems.question: For which b do the roots of (b+1)²3ˣ-(b+2)3⁻ˣ+2b+1=0 have opposite signs?
problems.idea: Put t=3ˣ. Opposite signs of x mean two positive t-roots on opposite sides of 1.
formulas: For a positive-leading-coefficient quadratic, two positive roots straddle 1 when their product and sum are positive and F(1)<0.
steps: The degenerate case b=-1 gives at most one root and cannot qualify.
The product of the two t-roots is -(b+2)/(b+1)², so both positive roots require b<-2. Their sum is then automatically positive.
F(1)=b²+3b=b(b+3). To place 1 strictly between the roots, require -3<b<0.
Intersect with b<-2 to get -3<b<-2. In this range F(1)<0 also ensures distinct real roots.
Each t-root gives one x=log₃t, with opposite signs.
